title: Practical Electricity
seo_title: Secondary 4 Physics: Practical Electricity Worksheets (O-Level 6091 with Answers)
standard_text: Describe the use of the heating effect of electricity in appliances; recall and apply P = VI and E = VIt, together with P = I²R and P = V²/R; calculate the cost of using electrical appliances where the energy unit is the kWh; state the hazards of damaged insulation, overheating cables and damp conditions; explain the use of fuses and circuit breakers and the choice of fuse rating; explain the need for earthing metal cases and for double insulation; state the meaning of the terms live, neutral and earth and why switches and fuses are connected in the live wire (summary of the Singapore-Cambridge O-Level Physics 6091 syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Secondary 4 O-Level Physics worksheets on practical electricity: electrical power, energy and cost in kWh, fuses and circuit breakers, earthing, double insulation and safe wiring. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Fuses and switches go in the live wire.
body_html:
How to think about it

Power is the rate of transfer of electrical energy.

  • P = VI = I²R = V² ÷ R. E = VIt (J). Energy in kWh = power in kW × time in h; 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10⁶ J.
  • Cost = number of kWh × price per kWh (in Singapore, about 30 cents).
  • Choose a fuse rating just above the normal current. Fuses and switches go in the live wire.
  • Earth metal cases so a fault current blows the fuse; double-insulated appliances need no earth wire.
Example

A 1500 W hair dryer on 230 V. Current? Fuse (3 A, 5 A, 13 A)?

I = 1500 ÷ 230 = 6.5 A

Answer: 6.5 A, so a 13 A fuse

Example

A 2.4 kW heater is used for 30 min at 30 cents per kWh. Cost?

2.4 × 0.5 = 1.2 kWh

1.2 × 30

Answer: 36 cents

Common mistakes

  • Calling the kWh a unit of power. It is a unit of energy.
  • Choosing a fuse much larger than the normal current.
  • Putting the fuse or switch in the neutral wire.
  • Using minutes instead of hours when finding kWh.

faq.q: How do you calculate the cost of electricity?
faq.a: Change the power into kW and the time into hours, multiply to get kWh, then multiply by the price per kWh.

faq.q: How do you choose the right fuse?
faq.a: Work out the normal current with I = P ÷ V and choose the fuse with the next rating above it.

faq.q: Why is the earth wire important?
faq.a: If a fault makes a metal case live, the earth wire lets a large current flow to earth, which blows the fuse and makes the appliance safe.

items.q: What is the danger of overloading a socket with many appliances?
c: water conducts, so current may flow through the person
the cable overheats because of its resistance and may melt the insulation
a person could touch the live wire and get an electric shock
the large current overheats the cables and may start a fire
items.e: Overloading a socket with many appliances: the large current overheats the cables and may start a fire.

items.q: A rice cooker is rated 700 W, 230 V. Which fuse should be used: 1 A, 3 A, 5 A, 10 A or 13 A?
items.e: Normal current = 700 ÷ 230 = 3.04 A. Choose the smallest fuse rating just above this: 5 A.

items.q: What does the fuse do (or mean)?
c: provides a low-resistance path to earth so that a large current flows and blows the fuse if the metal casing becomes live
means the appliance is disconnected from the high p.d. when it is switched off
melts and breaks the circuit when the current is too large, protecting the cable from overheating
means the appliance has a plastic outer casing, so the user cannot touch live metal and no earth wire is needed
items.e: The fuse: melts and breaks the circuit when the current is too large, protecting the cable from overheating.

items.q: What does the earth wire do (or mean)?
c: provides a low-resistance path to earth so that a large current flows and blows the fuse if the metal casing becomes live
switches off automatically when the current is too large and can be reset
melts and breaks the circuit when the current is too large, protecting the cable from overheating
means the appliance is disconnected from the high p.d. when it is switched off
items.e: The earth wire: provides a low-resistance path to earth so that a large current flows and blows the fuse if the metal casing becomes live.
